about.after_hours: Sand is also looking for work right now, so this chat doubles as a cover letter.

fun_facts: Has been a notary public and a passport acceptance agent at a U.S. embassy.
Has worked at U.S. embassies in three countries: Panama, Cyprus and Honduras.
Kept Autodesk Backburner render farms running for a game studio.
Did IT for a casino, where compliance meant state gaming regulations.
Deployed an entire network, servers and all, for a company acquisition.
Built a dog bloodwork guide with profiles for 70+ breeds.
Studied game and simulation programming, then went on to ship real game mods.

beats.question: is Sand open to work?
say: **Yes.** Sand is looking for work right now, as a software engineer or creative technologist.
The pitch: production web, desktop and AI apps shipped end to end, on top of ten years of IT operations and federal-sector work handling sensitive identity data under strict privacy rules.

beats.question: what does Sand do by day?
tell me more about LadderStar
say: **LadderStar** (ladderstar.com) is a live AI interview platform. Candidates audition in a real-time, voice-to-voice room running on Google's **Gemini Multimodal Live API**.
bullets: A full product: job board, public talent and employer profiles, real-time messaging, an admin console and blog publishing
Token-based employer screenings with consent-gated recording
Firebase auth with rules-unit-tested Firestore security rules, plus Stripe billing
outro: Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Firebase, the Gemini Live API, Stripe and Vercel.

beats.question: has Sand actually built with AI?
say: Plenty. Hands-on with models from **Anthropic**, **Google** and **OpenAI**, plus DeepSeek, Hugging Face, Replicate, Ollama and llama.cpp.
bullets: Real-time voice interfaces, like LadderStar's voice-to-voice audition room
Multi-agent orchestration, tool calling and the **Model Context Protocol**
RAG, prompt and context engineering, and evaluations

beats.question: what's BloodHound?
say: A local-first guide for dog owners. It turns flagged canine lab results into conservative nutrition notes and structured questions to bring to a vet.
outro: Deterministic rules, an explicit non-diagnostic scope, and no server-side health data. Live at **bloodhound-nine.vercel.app**.

Automated server operations over SFTP and RCON
A custom launcher client, a Discord bridge, and the Java gameplay mods the server runs on

say: Years of hands-on IT before the federal work:

beats.question: any open source?
say: **Port Visualizer**, MIT-licensed: a Windows desktop app for inspecting and managing active TCP/UDP ports.
bullets: Live connection diffing, process-grouped views and safe process termination, with UAC elevation and core system processes protected
Queries the native PowerShell API and falls back to netstat parsing when security policy blocks it
CI runs lint, type-check, unit tests, build and installer packaging on every push

beats.question: hold on, airship mods?
say: Two published mods for Create: Aeronautics, on **CurseForge** and **Modrinth**: procedural delivery contracts with physics-compiled cargo, and a preflight tool that simulates mass, lift, balance and thrust torque.
outro: A real bug from players: a server-thread ConcurrentModificationException. Sand moved chunk generation off-thread behind a tick-paced work queue and added regression tests.
